chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Amr ibn Shimr, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who drinks a drink of wine, Allah will not accept his prayer for seven days, and the one who becomes intoxicated, his prayer will not be accepted from him for forty mornings.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the acceptance of prayer for someone who drinks wine or gets drunk?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the spiritual consequence of consuming khamr on the validity of daily prayers, distinguishing between the act of drinking (seven days) and the state of intoxication (forty days). This ruling highlights the concept of 'ghaflah' (heedlessness) as a barrier to divine acceptance, emphasizing that ritual purity extends beyond physical cleanliness to include the clarity of the heart and mind. The distinction underscores the severity of intoxication in Shia jurisprudence as a major sin that temporarily suspends the efficacy of obligatory worship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar, from Amro Bin Shimr who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who drinks a wine drink, his Prayer would not be Accepted from him for a week, and the one get intoxicated, his Prayer would not be Accepted from him for forty days’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from ‘Amr ibn Shamir who has said the following: “

I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘If one drinks one sip of wine Allah will not accept his Salat (prayer) for seven (days) and if one becomes drunk his Salat (prayer) is not accepted for forty days.’”
